state: The question concerns draft source/deployment semantics, not shipping a library. Current selection pulls complete executable packages through local imports, including their resources; bound interfaces instead supply extracted owner-qualified schemas. The tested graph for a mailroom has ten owner packages and nine deployment bindings. Email is used by required notices. The other keys are billing, membership ingress, payment, billing ingress, documents, sales ingress, qualified sales and commissions. Mail permits externally documented paid entitlement with no linked Term and disables fee invoicing per service, but these data branches do not remove dependencies. A structural Charge import and a static invoice-finance role import contribute accidental invoice inclusion. The remaining membership Term plus eligible_term read genuine live records and enforce current paid/customer/seat/time/paused/revoked facts; a cached value or an asynchronous check cannot simply substitute. Membership links referral/affiliate owners. Paid memberships and invoiced fees remain required when chosen: freeze one fee identity, preserve owner validation and privacy, reconcile uncertain billing, correlate outcomes and keep parcel dispatch determined only by carrier evidence. Owners alone mutate their own data, and their hooks/canonical operations cannot be lost. Language contracts are revisable without implementation compatibility, but avoid schemas copied into consumers, wrapper manifests and unsupported pruning claims. Existing version/provider release gates preserve admitted or uncertain old work and pending schedules before any service is disconnected. These are source traces; no runtime equivalence, speed or fee savings have been measured.

closure.instructions: Assess four equally scoped ways forward and choose the most proportionate contract for required independent/manual and optional integrated use.

criteria.whole: Maintain mandatory full-owner resource closure and clearly expose it in generated installation documentation. This is semantically conservative and adds nothing to source or runtime contracts, but manual evidence and no-fee forwarding still require unused commercial resources.
criteria.values: Adopt owner-free closure solely for structural values and immutable role identities, carrying canonical types/constraints/assets rather than copied definitions; get Charge from the existing bound schema. Keep live model/function ownership whole. It fixes some excess dependency edges but leaves the live membership graph and Mail billing requirement, so it only partly meets the setup goal.
criteria.partition: Refactor real optional commercial processes into selectable packages using only current owner calls and typed events. Canonical stored data, policies, locks and CRUD stay owned once. Successful integration needs properly authorized handoffs and retained hooks/history rather than cosmetic file splitting or foreign writes. Avoids optional-binding semantics if feasible, but creates source boundaries/bridges and still needs a complete equal-outcome witness.
criteria.optional: Allow the selected app to explicitly list binding keys permitted absent while preserving every owner declaration and extracted schema. Absence outside that list remains deployment failure. Present providers retain normal behavior. An attempted send through an allowed-but-missing provider rejects atomically as rule_failed, leaving no domain writes or intents; absence never counts as skipping/success. The manual/no-fee paths need only providers they actually invoke, and full commercial use configures its adapters. Old unresolved work prevents disconnect until the established pinned-namespace/drain gate passes. This offers bounded deployment optionality without pruning or duplicate owners, but adds a real new contract and does not reduce executable source context.
